due_when.clears_when: A session measuring a condition its own cycle has been remediating states WHICH SHA its control was graded at, and why that sha is uncontaminated. Cheap, mechanical form: grade the negative control in a worktree at the last commit before the current cycle's work began, and record that sha beside the result -- scripts/ops/uncarried_specs.py --self-test --strict-negative is a worked example (it REFUSES to pass unless the known-stranded artifact grades un-carried on a pre-remediation tree). !! DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY DROPPING THE CONTROL: the contaminated control still passed, so removing it loses the only thing that caught the under-count. !! AND A PROBE WITH NO NEGATIVE CONTROL AT ALL IS WORSE THAN A CONTAMINATED ONE -- it cannot be wrong in a way anyone notices.
